claim: The overlay subclasses the game window procedure (SetWindowLongPtrW GWLP_WNDPROC) and swallows WM_INPUT raw input while the hub is open, implying the game uses Win32 Raw Input for mouselook; the repo also claims a global cursor-control gate at 0x1427030c8.
evidence: Overlay.cpp:356 if (msg == WM_INPUT) return ::DefWindowProcW(h, msg, w, l); :422 SetWindowLongPtrW(gameWnd_, GWLP_WNDPROC, ...)
game_build_compatibility: UNKNOWN: repo records no game version, Steam buildid, exe hash or build check; it only states a ~112 MB x64 Steam exe with SteamStub v3.1 + Denuvo (docs/reverse-engineering.md:12,21-29). Our exe is 117732784 bytes (~112.3 MiB), consistent but not proof of 1.0.8874.0 / build 3095001. The WndProc/raw-input approach is build-independent; the cursor gate RVA is hardcoded.
verification_method: Static read of repo source. That the game consumes WM_INPUT is an inference (game-side claim = HYPOTHESIS for our build).
limitations: No game-internal input/action-mapping structures, controller (XInput) or per-player input routing are mapped - a key gap for a second local/remote player.
next_experiment: Static import/string check of our exe for RegisterRawInputDevices / XInput usage to map the input path.
